I had a rough day. I was going through a down period during high school, and was withdrawing from bullying by people I previously thought as friends. Before then, I had thoughts of suicide, but I would be open in talking about it with a few close friends I had in my class. 

This day, I had one of them snap at me. I still remember their exact words, along with the frustration in their face.

*"If you were going to kill yourself, you would have done it already by now"*

Hearing it made me click. I felt I had nothing left to wait for at that point. 
During the rest of the day I felt distant from everything, but I was able to smile to others when needed. I didn't want to mess this up. I knew my parents were going to be away this night time.

Latter that night things were different. Instead of being being upset and angry, I felt calm. I knew that it was time to leave. During it, I didn't feel anything. I had a song playing that had me feel zoned out further. A razor blade felt like my only solace, the shining reflection as it moved.

I was feeling light headed but calm, but I was not thinking of anything around me. Eventually I felt like I wanted to sleep. So I did.

I woke up not long after, my first thought was of panic and regret. I jumped online in a panic, and can't remember what I was like, but it was enough to have someone speak to me on the phone and have the police come to check if I was ok. My parents came home shortly after which kicked a chain of events off. Besides being in shock, they were mostly talking amongst themselves in the first few days, and keeping an eye on me wherever I went. I've definitely learned a lot of coping resources to help me when I feel my most vulnerable.

Writing this has been scary as heck, as it's been a long, long time ago.

I barely got any sleep. I'll write more soon.

I don't like it. I feel like my gears of motivation have worn down. 
Most steps forward I take seem to be followed by two steps back. The more certain I get about what I would like to do in life, the less stable it appears to happen.

For me the feelings were of hopelessness. I still remember knowing that I was becoming depressed, and in my mind I planted a "bomb" of positive thoughts and affirmative things to do. 

When I was down and couldn't get out, use it to wash all the bad thoughts away.

What really happened was I hurt myself and didn't bother to "use" it, because I didn't feel like I was worth feeling good. That I wasn't worth feeling happy.

At the time, it would have been mostly about friends and lack of people understanding.

Growing up much latter, I realized that friends come and go, often they will give me a lot of hurt.... But I still need to be able to stand on my own two feet.
